policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV renders the coordinated clause 'and have done wickedly'; the conjunction 'and' distinguishes the ketiv reading והרשענו from the qere without the conjunction.
ASV has the plural 'his words,' distinguishing ketiv דבריו from singular qere דברו.

ASV 'open thine eyes' does not distinguish the qere imperative פקח from the ketiv form פקחה; the Hebrew-gloss note concerns 'cause to fall' elsewhere in the verse and does not decide this unit, so the base fallback is retained.
ASV's main text reads 'to make an end of sins,' while the mapped textual-variant note identifies 'to seal up' as another reading; this distinguishes and selects qere ולהתם over ketiv ולחתם.
ASV renders the plural 'sins,' distinguishing ketiv חטאות from singular qere חטאת.
